Tom — thanks, and great questions. Answers (technical):

1) Egress allowlisting and management
- Supported: yes. On both VPC and on-prem packages, outbound egress from the runtime can be restricted to a customer-provided list of IP ranges and FQDNs.
- Management: the allowlist can be updated via an operator-facing CLI/API on the appliance; for VPC customers there is a console-backed allowlist and an API endpoint that accepts a signed CSV of CIDR ranges.
- Automation: we provide a minimal webhook-driven integration pattern (payload examples attached) so your network team can push changes from your CMDB.

2) Control plane connections
- Default behavior: the private deployment includes an optional control plane connector used only for telemetry (optional) and for retrieving signed license updates. This connector is disabled by default in air-gapped installs.
- Disablement: operators can disable all outbound control-plane calls via a single configuration flag in the local operator manifest. When disabled, signed artifacts must be applied via offline media and verified locally.

3) Patch & signature workflow for air-gapped installs
- Process: vendors (Redwood) publish signed patch bundles (SHA256 + detached PKCS7 signature). Your operators pull bundles to an isolated staging server, verify the signature using our published signing keys (provided in the attestation package), perform offline validation (checksum + smoke tests), then apply via the operator CLI.
- Timeline: critical security patches follow a 48-hour push cadence for customers on our private patch feed; air-gapped customers receive signed bundles and a recommended apply window (we provide notarized checksums and verification scripts).

4) Artifacts we can provide today (attached/uploaded)
- redwood-network-egress-diagram.pdf (diagram of permitted flows and internal ports)
- redwood-attestation-template.docx (operator attestation template for your legal team)
- redwood-deployment-dataflow.csv (example CSV export of allowed egress CIDRs)
- sample-webhook-payloads.txt (API integration examples)

Security notes:
- All signatures use RSA-4096 keys and we rotate signing keys per our key management policy; rotation events are communicated in advance.
- Telemetry payloads (when enabled) are encrypted and sent only over TLS 1.3 to customer-approved endpoints; by default we do not send model inputs or customer PII as telemetry.

I'll upload the three core artifacts to the Drive link Chloe mentioned and drop a DocuSign template for the attestation. Happy to walk through any of these on the call.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz

Redwood Inference

- We agreed control-plane connections are optional and will be disabled by default for your air-gapped nodes; Redwood will add the config flag text to the SOW.

Recommended SOW snippet (draft):
"Redwood shall not initiate any outbound network traffic from customer-managed air-gapped environments except as explicitly authorized by a written operator configuration or during scheduled maintenance windows with prior notice. Any telemetry or control-plane interactions shall be disabled by default and enabled only at the explicit direction of Customer."
